The breakthrough uses atomically thin materials and nanoscale engineering to enable optical computing that could dramatically accelerate AI processing and quantum computing applications while consuming far less energy than traditional electronic systems.

items.title: HSE Scientists Help Deliver World-First Hydrogen-Powered Jet Engine Test
items.summary: HSE scientists contributed to a world-first achievement in aviation by helping deliver a hydrogen-powered jet engine test at full take-off power with Rolls-Royce. This breakthrough represents a major advancement in net zero aviation technology, demonstrating that hydrogen can power commercial aircraft engines at the power levels required for takeoff, bringing sustainable aviation significantly closer to reality.

items.title: Scientists Discover Explosive 'Ruptoblasts' That Kill Cancer Cells in Minutes
items.summary: Researchers have discovered a new type of cell called 'ruptoblasts' in flatworms that can detonate and release compounds that kill nearby cells within minutes. This breakthrough discovery, published in Nature, reveals a previously unknown cellular mechanism that could potentially be harnessed for targeted cancer therapy, as the ruptoblasts can selectively destroy harmful cells while leaving healthy tissue intact.

items.title: Microsoft Unveils AI-Designed Quantum Chip with Majorana Breakthrough, Targets 2029 Commercial Systems
items.summary: Microsoft revealed a revolutionary quantum computing chip redesigned with AI assistance, achieving a 1000-fold performance improvement in Majorana qubit technology. The breakthrough involves using lead-based materials in specialized manufacturing processes, marking a critical milestone toward commercially viable quantum computers by 2029, directly competing with IBM and Google in the quantum race.

items.title: Monash University Creates First Complete Light-Based Computing Chip Using Valleytronics
items.summary: Scientists achieved a major breakthrough in photonic computing by creating the first complete on-chip system that generates, routes, and reads light-based information using quantum valley properties. The room-temperature device uses atomically thin materials and could revolutionize AI computing efficiency while reducing energy consumption by replacing electronic processes with ultra-fast optical computations.

items.title: Stanford Develops Room-Temperature Quantum Device Using Twisted Light for Entanglement
items.summary: Researchers overcame one of quantum technology's biggest hurdles by creating a quantum device that operates at room temperature, using twisted light to entangle photons and electrons. This breakthrough could enable smaller, cheaper quantum systems with applications in secure communications, future AI computing, and quantum networks without requiring extreme cooling.

items.title: NASA Roman Space Telescope Poised to Discover 100,000 Exoplanets in Revolutionary Search
items.summary: NASA's Roman Space Telescope is set to revolutionize alien world detection by discovering approximately 100,000 exoplanets—surpassing all previous missions combined. The advanced space observatory will use cutting-edge detection methods to peer deep into space, potentially identifying Earth-like worlds and expanding humanity's understanding of planetary formation and habitability across the cosmos.

items.title: Scientists Reverse Brain Aging with Innovative Nasal Spray Treatment
items.summary: Texas A&M researchers developed a groundbreaking nasal spray that appears to reverse brain aging by calming inflammation and restoring energy systems. After just two doses, memory and cognitive function improved for months, raising hopes for treating neurodegenerative diseases. This represents a major convergence of neuroscience and biotechnology in developing non-invasive brain rejuvenation therapies.

items.title: Microsoft Unveils AI-Designed Quantum Chip with 1000x Performance Breakthrough
items.summary: Microsoft announced its revolutionary Majorana 2 quantum computing chip, redesigned using AI tools for materials science. The breakthrough achieved a 1000-fold improvement in performance by solving how to use lead-based superconducting materials without degradation during manufacturing. This convergence of AI and quantum computing brings commercial quantum systems to 2029, potentially cracking problems in medicine, chemistry, and cybersecurity that would take conventional computers millennia.

items.title: NVIDIA Launches Cosmos 3: First Open Physical AI Foundation Model for Robotic Intelligence
items.summary: NVIDIA released Cosmos 3, the world's first fully open omnimodel with native vision reasoning and multimodal generation across text, image, video, ambient sound and action. Built on breakthrough mixture-of-transformers architecture, it enables robots, autonomous vehicles and AI agents to perceive, reason, plan and act in the physical world. The model represents the convergence of AI reasoning with physical reality, launching the Cosmos Coalition with leading AI labs to advance open world models.

items.title: China's Artificial Sun Breaks Fusion Density Barrier in Historic Quantum Leap
items.summary: China's EAST reactor achieved the density-free regime breakthrough, maintaining plasma stability at extreme densities previously thought impossible. Using AI-controlled millisecond-precision plasma management, researchers overcame a 70-year density barrier that has blocked commercial fusion. This represents convergence of AI control systems with fusion physics, offering a practical pathway toward unlimited clean energy and bringing fusion ignition significantly closer to reality.

items.title: IBM Commits $10 Billion for World's First Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computer by 2029
items.summary: IBM announced a five-year $10 billion investment to build the world's first large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computer by 2029. The initiative includes the first dedicated quantum wafer foundry in the U.S. through the new Anderon venture. With quantum advantage demonstrations expected in 2026 and real workloads already running on 90+ quantum systems globally, this marks the transition from quantum experimentation to practical quantum-powered civilization infrastructure.

items.title: Stanford's Room-Temperature Quantum Device Uses Twisted Light for Photon-Electron Entanglement
items.summary: Stanford researchers created a nanoscale optical device that operates at room temperature while linking quantum properties of light and electrons using twisted photons. This breakthrough overcomes the extreme cooling requirements that have limited quantum technology deployment, paving the way for smaller, cheaper quantum systems with applications in secure communications, AI computing platforms, and human-quantum interfaces. The convergence of room-temperature quantum effects with photonic manipulation represents a major step toward ubiquitous quantum technologies.
